sections.title: Story
sections.narration: You scroll feeds for hours each day. Centuries ago, hunters spent far less time comparing status. In the 1990s, Robin Dunbar found hunter‑gatherers groomed about 20 % of their day. So why does scrolling feel like a status hunt? Because dopamine spikes when we see highlights, a 2015 Harvard study showed. The result? Comparison drains energy and raises stress. In 2018, Penn researchers found limiting Facebook to 30 minutes cut depressive symptoms by 20 %. That's it. So next time you feel the urge to compare, remember you scroll
